findings: The preserved source asks for a Java min-heap implementation without directly using PriorityQueue and does not provide a fixed API, capacity, duplicate, empty-heap, or concurrency contract; the candidate keeps those missing details explicit as chosen contract rather than source facts.
The int-array complete-tree representation, parent/child index formulas, sift-up insertion, and sift-down deletion toward the smaller child correctly maintain the parent<=child min-heap invariant.

The implementation preserves duplicate values, handles Integer.MIN_VALUE and Integer.MAX_VALUE without subtraction-based comparison overflow, and throws NoSuchElementException for empty peek/poll as explicitly documented.

OpenJDK 21 validation covers directed empty/duplicate/extreme cases, 50000 deterministic mixed operations against an independent TreeMap multiset oracle, and a 200000-element drain against a separately sorted oracle.
Complexity discussion correctly identifies O(1) peek and O(log n) heap-path work while separately noting occasional O(n) dynamic-array growth and its amortized behavior.
The candidate distinguishes heap order from global array order and explains why poll must choose the smaller child, giving a useful mechanism-level invariant rather than only code.
The one-minute section contains six bullets rather than the house 3-5 guidance; this is a minor oral-format deviation, not a correctness or promotion hard failure.
